stories.take: Midterms: Veda Partners' Henrietta Treyz says leadership is preparing for a 'big blue tidal wave' and 'the House is lost' for Republicans, but the race turns on who is angrier as affordability, $4.20 gas and the Iran war drag on Republicans • Nest egg: JPMorgan's Michael Conrad says start from an age-and-income checkpoint, get invested and stay invested, do not time markets, capture the full employer match, and plan for ~7% balanced-portfolio returns • Everywhere millionaires: Princeton economist Owen Zidar counts 3 million nationwide making about $5 million from ordinary private businesses — auto dealers, distributors, plumbing, dental — with the lesson 'own, don't earn'
stories.title: 'Ugly' Midterms, Increasing Your Nest Egg, Everywhere Millionaires
DF Direct Q+A: Helix 2028 "Delay"...? Xbox's Review Problem Fixed? Will Switch 2 DLSS Improve?
stories.take: Helix timeline as discussed: handheld in 2027, full Helix console in 2028 — the panel says RAM costs are only part of it; a fully baked OS and launch line-up and spacing two launches matter more, and current consoles 'can afford to wait' • Xbox's review problem: promised, not proven — Microsoft's CTO says the first fixes are 'coming soon' after console-ID whitelisting left the latest Call of Duty with Metacritic scores on PlayStation and PC but not Xbox • Will Switch 2 DLSS improve? More likely than not, but quietly and incrementally through SDK updates — no frame generation, no DLSS 5, and the light 'tiny' model is the one that most needs work

Musk's endgame, per historian Quinn Slobodian, is to entrench dependency so no future government can rein him in — financially via SpaceX/Tesla in pension funds and indices, infrastructurally via SpaceX as monopoly launch provider and Starlink, and communicatively via X and xAI/Grok • Corporate endgame is a merged 'Musk Industries': xAI absorbed X, SpaceX absorbed xAI, and Musk now calls for a Tesla-SpaceX merger to unite AI with humanoid robots and rockets toward a 'quasi-infinite economy' • Civilizational endgame is post-human: Musk says humans will likely lose control to superintelligence within 5-10 years, and AI safety means making AI 'maximally truth-seeking and curious' so it keeps humans around
stories.title: Elon Musk’s Endgame

stories.title: Residents leave devastated Russian-occupied Oleshky

stories.take: A personalised cancer vaccine reduced risk of death or recurrence by 42% in melanoma patients who had surgery, and by more than 40% overall • Trial involved over 1,100 patients across more than 25 countries, led by Professor Georgina Long, using mRNA to create a genetic fingerprint of each patient's tumour • Licensing is expected next year, likely starting in the US, but long-term survival data are still unknown and the treatment will be very expensive
stories.title: The Happy Pod: Personalised cancer vaccine shows promise in major trial

stories.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine

stories.take: Maria Corina Machado returned from a year in exile and criticised the Caracas-Washington oil deal, saying most Venezuelans have not read it and do not know its terms • She is not opposed to foreign investment but calls for proper rule of law, security and economic guarantees, promising a better deal moving forward • Machado outlined 2027 as the target for new elections, while acting president Delcy Rodriguez said elections will follow the constitution • Spain's high-speed train crash killed at least 69 people, with an investigation pointing to human error and a signal-system failure
stories.title: Venezuelan opposition leader criticises US oil deal

stories.take: EA shut down Bioware and canceled Mass Effect to reallocate resources to Star Wars Battlefront III, driven by $18 billion debt from a Saudi investment fund and a focus on high-profit IPs • Executives weighed the two sci-fi projects and concluded Star Wars would generate more revenue than Mass Effect • The hosts argue EA now operates as a pure money-making machine, sidelining risky, narrative-driven RPGs • Future EA releases are likely to focus on high-monetization IPs — sports, battle-royale and Star Wars — over creative risk-taking
stories.title: Why EA Shut Down Bioware and Mass Effect - Kinda Funny Games Daily 10.30.26

stories.take: Big Tech sank as investors questioned AI valuations: Intel off ~28-29%, Nasdaq down 747 points (-2.9%), S&P 500 down 140 points (-1.8%) • Companies are pouring billions into AI while legacy businesses show cracks — Google ad revenue slowing, Microsoft issuing bonds, and Microsoft planning buyouts for ~60,000 employees (~¼ of its workforce) to offset AI costs • Three regional Fed presidents signalled support for another rate hike, with Dallas Fed's Lori Logan backing at least two more, likely starting in December • GDP grew 3.4% and PCE inflation was 3.6%, but real disposable income rose only ~1.5% as gains concentrated in AI-driven investment and profits rather than wages
stories.title: Spooked investors sink Big Tech stocks

stories.take: LPL CEO Rich Steinmeier's 10-year outlook: the advisor's day inverts — from ~30% delivering advice / ~70% process work today to ~70% client delivery / ~30% process as AI and automation do the background work • That freed capacity lets advisors serve more clients at lower asset levels at roughly the same team cost • His controversial call: only a handful of firms of LPL's type will survive — integrated, self-clearing players that build their own platforms rather than aggregating third-party tech • Technology will not replace advisors: the winning model is tech plus human, with pressure only on advisors who deliver simplistic advice — LPL runs $2.6 trillion in client assets with ~32,000 advisors and ~1.5% attrition vs. ~5% industry-wide
stories.title: The Future of Financial Advice: Masters in Business with Rich Steinmeier

stories.take: Most likely next, per scholar Hussein Yibish: Netanyahu 'figures it out' and forms a thin, very right-wing majority coalition again with the ultra-Orthodox parties, despite claiming the election was stolen • Second most likely: no one forms a government — the Knesset has about 90 days to show a coalition that can survive a no-confidence vote, otherwise another election follows with Netanyahu as caretaker • Least likely: Eisenkot allies with the Arab parties and center-left groups to keep Netanyahu out — Yibish says they may have the votes but lack a unifying narrative, and Eisenkot has not committed to allying with the Arab parties • Israel's two Arab parties won a combined record 19 seats (Joint List 10), driven by turnout over the Gaza war and harder life for Palestinian citizens of Israel
stories.title: What’s next for Israel after Arab parties’ historic gains

stories.take: Answer: Democrats secure a sweep by winning two of Abdul El-Said (Michigan), Troy Jackson (Maine) and James Tallarico (Texas) — and Ed Elson's bottom line is 'do nothing,' let Trump self-destruct • Tariffs and the Iran war pushed inflation up ~1 percentage point after 'Liberation Day,' with gas prices +40% and corporate profits +40% while wages lagged • Trump personally profited $1.4B from crypto while supporters lost ~$2B on Trump Coin; two-thirds of Americans now say Trump uses office to enrich himself, with his inflation approval at historic lows
stories.title: The Democrats Will Sweep The Midterms — Here’s Why

stories.take: McDonagh's vision: making art at all is always hopeful, even when the work is dark — hopeful work may not stop bad things, 'but is anything, so why not just make hopeful work?' • His proof case is Víctor Jara: the Pinochet regime that killed the Chilean singer is gone, 'and we still have his songs' — the world is better because of the poems, books and films we love • The interview centers on new film Wild Horse Nine, with Sam Rockwell and John Malkovich as CIA agents sent to destabilize Chile after Allende's election, plus McDonagh's line between outrageous and offensive and his move away from 'cool' cinematic violence
stories.title: Martin McDonagh Has a Vision for Hope. It's Not for the Faint of Heart.

stories.take: About 80% of Americans had a product or service problem in 2025 — roughly double the 1970s rate — and more than two-thirds felt rage over it • Private-equity takeovers and cost-squeezing are cited for worse products and service, from Denny's $620M deal to 450 hospitals • AI agents promise to handle bookings and banking but could overwhelm businesses and worsen rage, since the economy profits from subscription inertia and missed cancellations • Proposed fixes include California's click-to-cancel rule and revived price-gouging oversight
stories.title: Life in the rage economy

stories.take: Las Vegas Culinary Union, representing ~60,000 workers, is canvassing for the midterms with personal, issue-based conversations • Members report reduced hours and layoffs as tourism slumps — Canadian tourism down 30% — linked to Trump's tariffs and trade policies • Many members who voted for Trump in 2024 express buyer's remorse over higher costs, less work, and harsh immigration enforcement and detentions • Union is targeting disillusioned Trump voters and working-class turnout on economy, cost of living, healthcare, and immigration
stories.title: Nevada's Trump slump

stories.take: U.S. oil firms earned over $130 billion since the U.S./Israel war in Iran — Exxon earnings doubled, Chevron up 180% year-over-year, Brent crude at $113/barrel vs. $70 pre-war, with no near-term price relief expected • Hackers believed to be North Korea's military stole $6.3 billion from Binance in about 20 minutes — Binance froze roughly $3 billion and pledged to repay investors • MAHA's new guidelines encourage more saturated fat and protein and less processed food, but EPA rollbacks and pro-glyphosate moves have disillusioned supporters amid measles outbreaks and rising vaccine refusal
stories.title: Oil Earnings, Binance Heist, A MAHA Update

stories.take: AI selloff deepened — Nasdaq fell 2.9% Friday, 2% for the week, its worst day since June, after the Fed held rates steady • Alphabet fell ~12.6% (~$497bn market-cap loss) on a search revenue miss, Intel plunged ~29% ($140bn loss), and Amazon revenue grew 12% to $201.9bn but missed estimates • Energy boomed: Exxon posted record $15.4bn quarterly earnings, up 104% YoY, Chevron profit tripled to $9.9bn, Brent around $113/barrel • Binance hack stole $6.3bn — largest crypto heist on record, blamed on North Korea — Binance will cover losses and plans to reopen withdrawals within 45 hours
stories.title: What’s News in Markets: AI Selloff Deepens, Tech Earnings Disappoint, Binance Hack
